content.body:
In 1934 the French introduced the SA mle 34 as a replacement for the outdated 37 mm infantry Canon mle 16 TR. Despite its small caliber, the 317 g AP round had impressive performance out to 600 m range. It was so lightweight that it was found to be too flimsy for towing and normally was handled using horses. It was widely distributed and became the most common AT gun in the French army. After 1940, the Germans deployed them to local garrisons and police units throughout conquered territories.
The SA mle 34 (the "Samel 34") is an average quality tank gun but with a couple of very redeeming features. Like most AT guns, it fires very flatly, but the Samel 34 has in-sight range adjustment, meaning that if you can pre-set the range, you can duel confidently at ranges out to (and past) 1000 m, exceptional for such a small caliber gun. Therefore, don't hesitate to start shooting at long distances; you may get the enemy tank to halt to try to find you while you relocate.
It sits quite low on its mount, and is also quite stable shot-to-shot for tight groupings so feel free to pick your shots, particularly at smaller vulnerable spots on enemy tanks like driver slots and gunsights.
Unfortunately there is no HE round for the gun, so if engaging an enemy prime mover, try to hit the wheel hubs to cause a flip or roll, otherwise surviving infantry will be hunting you down very quickly.
The Samel also limbers (undeploys) and moves fast, so relocate frequently to prevent the enemy from figuring out where you are.
CREW POSITIONS: 1 Commander 2 Gunner
